A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete 68-page contents, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original numerical simulations of matrix and Markov games, with estimation errors presented in Figures 1–2 and Table 1.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original matrix-game and Markov-game simulations and their results in Figures 1–2 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same QRE estimation, confidence-set construction, transition estimation, and reward-recovery procedures. The appendix parameter-selection method is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two matrix-game setups and the same four-state, six-step Markov-game setting. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated external baselines. The newly cited Tang and Waugh works appear only in related-work discussion, without corresponding comparison experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same sampling procedures, dimensions, regularization settings, and error metrics. Sample sizes remain 10^3–10^6 for matrix games and 10^4–10^5 for Markov games.

E4.justification: The existing sample-size, identifiability, and time-step analyses are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 repetitions and 95% confidence intervals for the simulations. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information changes.

E6.justification: All plot panels, Table 1 entries, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, at N=100,000, both report reward error 1.4398 ± 0.0499 and QRE error 2.41×10^-3 ± 1.41×10^-4.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, identifiability conditions, convergence bounds, and proofs are unchanged. Appendices A–D match exactly; Definition 3.7 merely changes position relative to Algorithm 2.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2 contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reward identifiability, confidence-set estimation, the Markov-game extension, and theoretical and empirical validation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of partial identifiability, reward and QRE errors, and state-coverage requirements remain unchanged. The discussion of future extensions introduces no new limitation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The Google Colab disclosure, experimental hyperparameters, implementation descriptions, and appendix parameter-selection guidance are retained. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 adds Tang et al. (2024) and Waugh et al. (2013), with corresponding references. It distinguishes policy imitation and regret-based inverse-equilibrium behavior prediction from the paper's QRE-based payoff and reward recovery.

P1.justification: Section 1.3 gains a short discussion of Tang et al. and a comparison paragraph about Waugh et al. The remaining prose and section hierarchy are retained, with an updated version/date stamp.

P2.justification: Reflow moves Algorithm 2 from page 18 to 19 and Table 1 from page 30 to 31, and changes Figure 2's placement relative to Section 4.2. Figure content, captions, and table structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added acknowledgment and comparison of Waugh et al. clarify the relationship to earlier inverse-equilibrium research, while the Tang et al. discussion distinguishes policy imitation from reward recovery. These additions improve attribution and research positioning. The benefit is limited because the methods, theoretical support, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
